title: MCP Descriptor Integrity Design v1 — Rig Relay
design_objective: Every MCP tool descriptor must be cryptographically verified before any handler is invoked. Descriptor changes must be detected, produce evidence, and trigger refusal until re-verified. This prevents tool poisoning, shadowing, and rug-pull attacks at the MCP protocol layer.

descriptor_version.generation: Monotonic counter per tool. Starts at 1. Incremented on every verified descriptor change.

descriptor_hash.canonical_input: JSON-serialized dict of {name, description, input_schema, server_identity} with sort_keys=True

mutation_class.values: read_only | writes_evidence_only | writes_temp_only | unknown | FILE_WRITE | FILE_DELETE | WORKTREE_CHECKPOINT

allowed_roots.description: Paths the tool is authorized to access. $WORKSPACE_ROOT resolves at request time.

content_light_classification.note: No MCP tool should produce secret_bearing or forbidden_raw output. If detected, refusal is mandatory.

fields.previous_descriptor_hash: SHA256 of previous version (null for v1)

registration_flow.step_1: At RigMCPServer.__init__(), iterate all MCPTool instances from models.py READ_ONLY_TOOLS + GATED_TOOLS.
registration_flow.step_2: For each tool, call compute_tool_provenance_hash(tool.model_dump()) to generate descriptor_hash.
registration_flow.step_3: Store in self._tool_registry: dict[str, ToolRegistryEntry] where key is descriptor_hash and value includes tool reference, descriptor_version, created_at.
registration_flow.step_4: Also store self._tool_index: dict[name, descriptor_hash] for O(1) name→hash lookup.
registration_flow.step_5: Run classify_tool_descriptor_suspicious() on every registered descriptor. Flagged descriptors → log warning + emit governance telemetry. Do not exclude from registry (they need to be in the registry to be detected), but mark them as suspicious in the registry entry.
registration_flow.step_6: Emit rig.relay.mcp.descriptor.registered telemetry event with descriptor_hash, tool_name, tier, suspicious flag, and registration time.

dispatch_flow.step_1: call_tool(name, arguments) receives a tool call request.
dispatch_flow.step_2: Look up tool by name in self._tool_index to get registered descriptor_hash.
dispatch_flow.step_3: Re-compute provenance hash of the current in-memory tool descriptor.
dispatch_flow.step_4: Compare re-computed hash with registered hash.
dispatch_flow.step_5a_match: If hashes match → proceed to dispatch (after roots, content-light, auth checks).
dispatch_flow.step_5b_mismatch: If hashes Mismatch → refuse. Return refusal envelope with: refusal_code='descriptor_integrity_failure', refusing_hash=recomputed_hash, registered_hash=registered_hash, descriptor_version=N+1 (incremented). Emit rig.relay.mcp.descriptor.drift telemetry event. Log at WARNING level.
dispatch_flow.step_5c_unknown: If name not in registry → refuse with refusal_code='unknown_tool'.

rug_pull_detection.trigger: On every tools/list response and on every descriptor integrity check during dispatch.
checks: compare current descriptor_hash with registered hash
check if readOnlyHint changed from true to false on a tier 3+ tool
check if description byte size increased more than 2x between versions
rug_pull_detection.response_on_detection: Exclude tool from tools/list response. Emit rig.relay.mcp.descriptor.rug_pull telemetry event with: tool_name, previous_hash, current_hash, suspicious_reasons[], detector_version. Log at ERROR level.

attestation_record.verification: On startup, replay attestation log. Verify hash chain continuity. Gaps → log warning.
